definitions: To start again on a plan or idea from the very beginning, often because the previous attempt failed or was unsatisfactory.
To rethink an approach or design from scratch after an initial failure.
examples: Our first proposal was rejected, so we have to go back to the drawing board.
The prototype didn't work, meaning it's time to go back to the drawing board.
After the project failed, the team had no choice but to go back to the drawing board.
lemma: go back to the drawing board
source: go back to the drawing board
